name: Jehohanan
overview: Jehohanan was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as a priest and descendant of Aaron. He is uniquely noted as the son of Amariah, situating him within the Levitical priesthood. His role as a priest underscores his participation in the religious leadership of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehohanan means 'YHWH has been gracious,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in God's grace. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:13, carries no indication of being divinely given beyond its traditional Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jehohanan as the son of Amariah, as noted in Nehemiah 12:13. No other family relationships beyond this paternal link are documented in the biblical record provided.
scriptureSignificance: Jehohanan's significance lies in his position within the Levitical priesthood, serving as a descendant of Aaron and thus part of the sacred lineage responsible for temple worship and religious duties. His identification in Nehemiah 12:13 highlights the continuity of priestly service during the post-exilic period, emphasizing God's ongoing grace through faithful priestly families. As a priest, Jehohanan represents the faithful transmission of covenantal responsibilities entrusted to the Levites.
